(SPOILER FREE SHORT REVIEW)

I found this game through a random video on YouTube and after watching it for 5 minutes I decided to buy it and play it myself. It is very fun and immersive from the very beginning. The gameplay is very intuitive, UI is clean, voice actors are great and it has an amazing vibe. The story had me on the edge of my seat up until the ending. Each of the mechanics present in the game is very detailed and it sucks that the game is so short you only get to use them once. They could've added more filler missions to make the game longer and allow us to utilize all the mechanics more. There is a lot of options and decisions you have to make during your walkthrough, but the story somehow only has one ending? I finished it after around 3.7 hours and immediately wanted to start again to check the other endings just to find out that there is nothing more? The finale is also very unsatisfying, dissapointing and will leave your mouth dry.

For me, the game overall is 8.5/10, 100% worth playing.

This is a pretty solid game, at least the first time around. I've only been through it once, but I am curious about how it will be after a few runs. It's definitely a bit shorter than I thought (this run was around 3 hours), and while I didn't do much research on it before buying it (other than reading the tags and brief parts of the description), it seemed a bit different than what I expected. I was kind of thinking you'd go through and help solve multiple cases, and just keep going that way with increasing difficulty and depth as you continue playing. It's not that. It sort of starts that way, but doesn't stay that way for long. It's VERY linear as far as I can tell, and while I think there are different outcomes based on player inputs, I have yet to try that. It's not the investigation game it's labeled as. It's still well put together and thought out, but I felt a little bit misled, as there is really only one single "case" that you're working on as the player, it just happens to include a few other cases that you work on in the tutorial stages. 

Without spoiling it, I think it's a good game, though I don't know if I would pay full price for it. I think if you could get it for under $10 USD it would be a much better value, personally. But, we'll see how it goes on the replay-ability of the game and that might change. I'm curious how different actions and responses affect the outcome of the game for sure. 

Soundtrack really buffed this game a lot too, it was really well timed and well orchestrated. 

My main complaint is some of the cutscenes are ridiculously long for what their substance is. There is basically no substance to most of them, it's just some sound effects and maybe the occasional spot of dialogue.

As someone else said in their review, it scratched an itch I didn't know I had, but I would've been much more excited to see some real investigating. Like phasmophobia, but you're the computer geek at this government intelligence agency. If you play through the first hour or so, you'll see sort of what I mean by that.

The Operator is one of the games that show the limitations of Steam's "Yes/No" model for review. It's a good game, it's solid, but it's got its limitations that you need to understand before you buy.

To put it briefly: The Operator is the videogame equivalent of a good B-movie thriller. As a puzzle game and narrative experience it "does the job". You will get about four hours worth of puzzles that are just difficult enough to make you feel smart, but nothing that is designed to resist you too long either. You'll get a scenario that follows the codes of the conspiracy thriller, but is strongly linear and doesn't do anything you haven't seen at least a few times before...

There are puzzle games out there that will make you forever regret that you aren't able to experience them for the first time once more. Obra Dinn, There is No Game, Chants of Sennaar...The Operator is not one of those. It hits all the right notes, but the performance isn't inspiring.

If you like the genre of puzzle and thriller, then by all means go for it. It is a good, solid game for those gamers whose expectations are appropriately set. But if you haven't played puzzle games for a while and are looking for an amazing, unforgettable experience? Try the others first and come back here when you're hooked to the genre.

While a very polished and well-crafted experience, this game has a number of fatal flaws that undermine and eventually irrevocably cripple your enjoyment of it.  Firstly, it's incredibly short.  I do understand that this tends to be the case for these kinds of games, crafting content for them is much more effort intensive than it is for other genres, but even by the standards of other games in this genre, you get very little playtime compared to its cost.  This is further exacerbated by a complete lack of replay value, as the story is completely linear and has no alternate endings, though there are a few pieces of content not central to the story that the player can find through their own initiative.  If you take nothing else from this review and do decide to buy the game, buy it on sale, the existing content doesn't really justify the price point.

To get into the real reasons this is a negative review, as money alone wouldn't have been enough to get me to write this, we need to first revisit the game's linearity.  The game does provide the illusion of choice, but none of the choices the player can make matter, and acting as though they do will inevitably see the game yanking on your leash and railroading you back to the single story it wants to tell.  This linearity continues to the mysteries that form the game's content, as they are designed so that the player is forced to solve them linearly as well.  Rather than providing multiple angles of attack, players must solve one specific part of a mystery before progressing to the next one, so for the most part you don't get that feeling of everything coming together as multiple clues and leads snap together into a single image, though there are exceptions to this.  I can't get too much into the ending without spoiling players, but it was abrupt, unsatisfying, and served to terminate any remaining sense of agency I had.  Everything I had accomplished was undone in an instant, in a way that felt, frankly, disrespectful and contemptuous to me as a player.  The entire point of a game, the thing that fully differentiates it from other forms of media, is that the person consuming it has agency, is not simply a passive observer but actively engages with and shapes the piece of media that they are consuming.  Of all the games I've played, this embraces that principle the least, and suffers for it.

The ultimate sin of The Operator, however, the one no detective game can be forgiven for, is its predictability.  I am in no way talented when it comes to mysteries.  When I play a detective game, read a mystery novel, or watch a movie in those genres, I am generally unable to put together the pieces ahead of time and figure out the twist before it is presented to me.  This was not the case with The Operator.  I was able to determine most of the major narrative twists well ahead of time, because they were fairly obviously telegraphed.  There were a few that were well done, and there were some that would have been very good if other obvious elements hadn't telegraphed them ahead of time.  Anyone playing this game will likely figure out its main narrative twists well before they are presented to the player, and that is truly tragic.

Pros:
Immersion: The narrative takes the lead in the game. As we solve puzzles and analyze evidence, an intriguing story unfolds with unexpected twists. If you like sci-fi plots and conspiracy theories, you'll find the immersion very appealing.
Nostalgia: Dealing with equipment and devices from the 90s is something much appreciated.

Cons:
Short Game: “The Operator” is relatively short compared to other titles. Some players may feel that the experience ends too soon.
Limitations: The game feels very structured and with little freedom of action where decisions are not taken into account. There are times when you feel that you just have to click the mouse and that you can't do anything else.

Conclusion: good concept, good idea, beautiful experience of interacting with computers from other times, but all this feels a bit short.

I'm giving this game a 'recommended' because my overall feelings are more positive than negative, but I definitely feel like the price doesn't match the value. [b]This feels like the first act of a game, not an entire one.[/b]

The few puzzles aren't very challenging, and you spend as much time reading manuals for them as doing them because you generally do each type once without getting to test your skills further. The conversations are very casual and not nearly carefully worded enough for cloak and dagger operations, which feels out of place for the severity of the events. Everybody constantly name drops each other, though I'm sure this is so you can research characters in the database as a curious player.

As for the plot itself, it foreshadows and delivers, using linear conversations with dialog choices that affect nothing, and while I found most of it predictable, I still enjoyed the ride. This is because while I've listed so many negatives just now, [i] the immersive presentation of this game is extremely satisfying. [/i]

The interfaces, animations, and voice acting all contribute to a fantastic game-feel that kept me enjoying my time. The experience of playing this game was precisely what I wanted from it, [i]It nails the style that hard![/i] Making me walk away from a game that objectively failed to meet most of my expectations with such a positive outlook for future releases is an impressive trick.

I can't in good conscience give this game a good review, but I also can't give it a poor review. It's times like this I wish Steam had a middle-ground review option. This game was very fun and scratched an itch I didn't know I had. However, labeling it as an investigation game or describing it the way it does is misleading. Yes, there is some investigation, but there's really only one singular crime to solve. The storyline is very linear and easy to guess. If it were marketed as a game about solving a singular crime, that would be accurate, but it misleads you in the description by stating, 'Investigate mysterious crimes. Use cutting-edge FDI software to dig for clues, solve puzzles, and uncover the truth.' This is incorrect. You only use most of the 'software' exactly once, after implying you should read the extensive manual that comes along with it. This is a game that you could probably finish within 2-3 hours, which also doesn't justify its price. Honestly, they could have dropped the mid-tier storyline and just made a game along the lines of Criminal Minds or CSI, where you use these tools to try to solve cases, and it would be infinitely more fun. I know I'm probably the outlier here with my review, and I will say I did enjoy what they had, but it just wasn't what they promised in their wording and descriptions (maybe I misunderstood some stuff, who knows). There does seem to be an open door for expansions in the future, but if they're along the same timeframe as this game and offer only 2-3 hours of playtime, they should drastically reduce the price because as it stands, it felt like an expensive tech demo.

四小时的游戏时间 总体上是个不错的作品
首先看题材分类就知道不是强调游戏性的作品，所以就当综合作品来评价描述吧
---------------------------------好评内容---------------------------------
1.首先要夸的是风格化的水平还可以，在平面演出上做到了统一以及小部分出彩。
2.惊喜感比较强，对于矛盾叙事不敏感或者游玩心情较为轻松的玩家来说，能够在不同章节的不同节点给出惊喜感，且节奏把握能力也不错，将玩家体验的游戏内几个简单系统控制在了刚好不会厌烦的程度。
3.结构简单清晰，五脏俱全：卡关的引导思考恰到好处。
4.谜题难度分布合理，作品中的解谜交互要素的难度比较梯度，部分要素比较新颖。
---------------------------------不足之处---------------------------------
1.对话逻辑：部分人物的行为和对话逻辑难以自圆其说。
2.程序的判断逻辑有优化之处：对话需要经过A再到B才能触发进程，然而玩家拥有直接选择B的能力，这类强制玩家操作顺序的情况会一定程度上影响体验。
3.许多人提到的问题：分支对话无意义，也就是对话系统本身无法对剧情起到关键性分支作用，本身系统其实也是支持这种功能，但或许因为工期等其他缘故，制作组并没有加入这些内容。（或许拆弹专家是一个实验）

Overall enjoyable. Decent interface and storyline, good variety of puzzle mechanics, low to medium difficulty and complexity.

I'm usually not a fan of dialogue choices and multiple endings, so I didn't know how to feel when I found out this game [i]doesn't[/i] have alternative endings.  Like another user put it, it really felt like I had reached the "bad ending", and that I was supposed to make different choices.  But playing through a second time did not change the outcomes aside from slightly different dialogue, and seeing one or two subtle hints I had missed the first time around.

And the developer has confirmed that it's not intended to be replayable (see the dev's [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1771980/discussions/0/4511002214535949429/]community post[/url])

The interface is quite well done, with a variety of technical mechanics.  The in-game documents and user manuals are quite impressively believable in style, while staying relevant to the gameplay, and to the storyline.  I quite enjoyed the [spoiler]"Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes"[/spoiler] style puzzle.

I was a little disappointed that the terminal was so limited, but given this is a relatively small game, that's understandable.

At times, especially at the start, it felt like a bit of information overwhelm moving too quickly, but it generally seems to be quite forgiving (though I haven't tested what happens if you don't answer a call, or fail to [spoiler]defuse the bomb[/spoiler]).

Often it felt a bit too heavy on the handholding.  [spoiler]The "watch me."  "Are you watching me?" prompts for the scripted surveillance made me giggle[/spoiler].  Most of the big reveals were heavily hinted at early on so I knew long before the characters themselves knew.  There were a couple that surprised me though.

The voice acting was quite good.  As was the sound design, and animations.  There's quite a few unskippable animations but they're generally done quite well and relevant to the storyline or puzzles.

Overall decent little game.  First playthrough took me just about under ~6hrs at a meandering pace (and not keeping track of breaks).  Would play a sequel if it's ever made.
